messages:
maria: Hit a repeatable crash in the Python SDK when the server replies with Content-Type: application/json; charset=\"\". json.loads(resp.text) raises even though resp.content is valid JSON bytes.

kevin: Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact headers?

maria: Minimal repro (sync):
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
# server returns 400 with header: Content-Type: application/json; charset=\"\"
resp = c._session.request('POST', 'https://internal.test/errors', json={'x':1})
# client calls json.loads(resp.text) and raises JSONDecodeError
```

julia: Root cause: httpx/requests decoding chokes on an explicit empty charset token. Short term fix: stop relying on resp.text when charset is missing/empty. Proposed _parse_error flow:
1) if content-type looks like json, try resp.json() inside try/except
2) if that fails, do json.loads(resp.content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
3) on final failure, raise ClientError with raw_body = resp.content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace') and headers = dict(resp.headers) and set the original decode exception as __cause__.

kevin: Concrete plan: update ClientError dataclass (and AsyncClientError parity) to include raw_body, headers, status_code, request_url as small string/int fields; update .pyi stubs for typing; add unit tests for empty charset, missing charset, and non-utf8 bytes; make tests robust to httpx raising JSONDecodeError/DecodingError/ValueError by asserting cause.__class__.__name__ in an allowed set. I'll open a PR.

ci-bot: queued CI for branch kevin/sdk-charset-fallback (unit, mypy, integration)

maria: I'll attach a tiny Flask mock and a failing curl to the PR so CI can run against it locally.

kevin: PR created with code + tests + changelog. Preserving original exception as __cause__ so Sentry shows underlying error.

ci-bot: CI green, merged.

julia: nice. Add a short DX onboarding note: when reporting SDK errors include raw_body and headers to help triage charset issues.

maria: Verified local e2e against the mock, sync and async tests pass. Closing thread — thanks!
